terms.meaning: The Amazon's tropical rainforest, the world's largest.
Grasslands of South America: Llanos (Orinoco, Venezuela), Campos (Brazil), Pampas (Argentina).
The joint river system of the Parana, Paraguay and Uruguay.
A cowboy who rears cattle on the Pampas.
A name for South America, as people live on the coasts and the interior is nearly empty.
The milky sap of rubber trees in the Amazon forests.

items.name: Location of South America
items.formula: 12°N to 56°S and 35°W to 81°W; mostly in the Southern Hemisphere.
items.example: The Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn cross it; it is triangular.

items.name: Size of South America
items.formula: Fourth largest continent: 178.4 lakh sq km, 5.42 times India.
items.example: 13 countries: Brazil largest, French Guyana smallest; Bolivia and Paraguay have no coast.

items.name: Four physical divisions
items.formula: Andes Mountains, Eastern Highlands, Central Lowlands, Western Coastal Plains.
items.example: The Central Lowlands hold the Amazon, Orinoco and La Plata basins.

items.name: The Andes
items.formula: The world's longest mountain chain, 6440 km along the Pacific, in the Ring of Fire.
items.example: Highest peak: Aconcagua (6,960 m), on the Argentina-Chile border; rich in copper and tin.

items.name: Angel Falls
items.formula: The world's highest waterfall (974 m), in the Guyana Highlands.
items.example: The Guyana and Brazilian Highlands are old rocks like the Deccan.

items.name: The Amazon
items.formula: 6450 km from the Andes; the largest river in the world, with more than 1,000 tributaries.
items.example: Lake Titicaca (Bolivia) is the highest lake in the world.

items.name: Climate of South America
items.formula: The Amazon basin is hot and wet, with convectional "afternoon" rains.
items.example: East of the Andes is a rain shadow; Atacama (Chile) is the driest place, with no rain for 200 years.

items.name: Trees of the rainforest
items.formula: Hardwoods like mahogany and ebony, and rubber trees.
items.example: Brazil's south-east coast has deciduous forest.

items.name: Animals of South America
items.formula: "Continent of Birds": the condor, and the flightless rhea. Anaconda, jaguar, puma, piranha.
items.example: Llama and alpaca are used by local people; the Galapagos have giant tortoises.

items.name: Crops of South America
items.formula: Only about 10% of land is farmed: maize (native), wheat in Argentina and Chile, potato in the Andes.
items.example: Rice grows along the Brazilian coast.

items.name: Brazil's coffee
items.formula: Brazil is the world's largest coffee producer, the "Coffee pot of the world".
items.example: Rio de Janeiro is the "Coffee port of the world".

items.name: Livestock and fishing
items.formula: Pampas cattle (Argentina was once the top beef exporter); sheep on Patagonia.
items.example: Peru and Chile have the best fishing grounds.

items.name: Towns in South America
items.formula: About 80% of people live in towns, against a world average of 47%.
items.example: Uruguay is highest (93%) and Guyana lowest (36%).

items.name: Population growth
items.formula: Birth rate 21 per 1000, like the world's; death rate 6, below the world's 9.
items.example: So natural increase is faster than the world average.

mistakes.text: Llanos are in Venezuela, Campos in Brazil and Pampas in Argentina.
The Amazon is the largest river in the world, but the Andes are the longest mountain chain.
The rhea is a large bird that can't fly; the condor is the biggest flying bird.
